exercises.prompt: You are given cards, a list of card records of shape {'name', 'archetype', 'atk', 'def', 'level'}. Implement cards_at_level(cards, level) so it returns a list of the 'name' values of every card whose 'level' equals the given level, in the list's original order. cards_at_level(cards, 8) is ['Blue-Eyes White Dragon', 'Blue-Eyes Alternative Dragon', 'Dark Magician of Chaos']. exercises.solution:
def cards_at_level(cards, level):

exercises.prompt: You are given cards, a list of card records of shape {'name', 'archetype', 'atk', 'def', 'level'}. Implement deck_summary(cards, archetype) so it returns one report line about that archetype, formatted exactly as '<archetype>: <n> cards, top ATK <atk> (<name>)' — deck_summary(cards, 'Dark Magician') is 'Dark Magician: 3 cards, top ATK 2800 (Dark Magician of Chaos)'. Use the singular '1 card' when the archetype has exactly one card. If two of its cards tie for the highest atk, name the one that appears first in the list, so deck_summary(cards, 'Blue-Eyes') is 'Blue-Eyes: 2 cards, top ATK 3000 (Blue-Eyes White Dragon)'. If the archetype has no cards — including when the list is empty — return '<archetype>: no cards' instead.
exercises.solution:
def deck_summary(cards, archetype):
    owned = [c for c in cards if c['archetype'] == archetype]
    if not owned:
        return f'{archetype}: no cards'
    top = max(owned, key=lambda c: c['atk'])
    label = '1 card' if len(owned) == 1 else f'{len(owned)} cards'
    return f"{archetype}: {label}, top ATK {top['atk']} ({top['name']})"
